payload.retro_drained: Retro DEFERRED (owner ruling, no retro now). Inbox carried whole to the post-i9 retro. i8c reopens the abandoned i8b-phone-connect to finish in-flight work; design INHERITED from that iteration's evidence.
payload.goal: The board gets a top-middle toolbar; a phone-connect icon renders a locally-encoded QR in the details pane so the owner scans to pair the phone lane - making the from-away bless testable for the first time.
payload.pulled_in:
INHERITED from the abandoned i8b-phone-connect (blessed M1 + M2 design by pointer + delta):
- A top-middle board toolbar of small icons: a greyed book placeholder (until i6) and an active phone-connect icon.
- The connect action: clicking phone-connect generates the ntfy topic pair, writes ~/.se/<project>/phone.json (enabled), and renders a QR in the details pane, ENCODED LOCALLY (the topic is the credential, never sent to an external service).
- Dependency is free (se.adr-install-over-zerodep): QR encoder vendored or hand-rolled; one-click install is the law.
- The config-write amendment (owner-confirmed): the engine writing phone.json amends adr-phone-secret-machine-local.
FROM this session: i8c runs in its OWN worktree and now SHOWS + BLESSES on the board (projectState worktree-aware, offer in the shared dir, Gate.bless finds the worktree instance, board no longer spawns git per poll, worktree is not a separate tab - all tested).
payload.left_out:
- The book itself + its open action (i6 - the icon ships greyed).
- Other toolbar icons (future).
- Non-ntfy channels.
- The i8 bless mechanics (unchanged).
- QR decoding / the inbound side (the phone app subscribes; we only ENCODE).
- Live owner-physical pairing (raid-phone-live-pairing).
